# Part I — Getting started

What jayecu is, how to install the studio, a tour of it, the first connection to an ECU, and a checklist from a new box to a first start. Start here if jayecu is new to you.

- **[1 How to use this manual](01-using-this-manual.md)** — This chapter tells you how the manual is laid out, what the marks and conventions in it mean, and how to find the one page you need.
- **[2 The system at a glance](02-system-overview.md)** — A jayecu system is an ECU running firmware, jayecu Studio on your computer, a definition that tells the studio what the firmware contains, and your own files: the tune and the layout.
- **[3 Installing jayecu Studio](03-installing-studio.md)** — Jayecu Studio comes as one AppImage file on Linux and as an installer on Windows, keeps your tunes in a data folder that updates never touch, and can update itself.
- **[4 A tour of the studio](04-studio-tour.md)** — Jayecu Studio is the program on your PC that shows what the ECU is doing and changes its tune. This chapter names every part of its window and says what each menu item and button does, and when it is available.
- **[5 First connection](05-first-connection.md)** — Plug the ECU into the computer, press connect, and the studio finds it, opens its project, reads its tune and shows you it live.
- **[6 Quick start — box to first start](06-quick-start.md)** — The shortest safe path from a new ECU to an engine that starts and idles, as a checklist of eight stages, each pointing to the chapter that explains it in full.
